A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CViT research, despite the changed title and emphasis. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across the reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original CViT experiments on advection, shallow-water, and Navier-Stokes problems, including benchmark results and architectural ablations in the main text and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds CViT diffusion-reaction results and a latent-grid resolution study, reported in Tables 3 and 6 and Appendix F.

M1.justification: As written, the encoder initialization changes from z0 = zagg in v1 Section 4 to z0 = LN(zagg) in v2 Section 3.1, adding normalization before the encoder stack. Patchification, Perceiver temporal aggregation, normalized grid interpolation, and query-wise cross-attention otherwise remain. Renaming the interpolation parameter from epsilon to beta is not a method change.

E1.justification: v2 adds PDEBench's coupled two-dimensional diffusion-reaction task, predicting activator and inhibitor fields. This materially extends evaluation beyond the retained advection, shallow-water, and Navier-Stokes tasks to reaction-diffusion dynamics (Section 4.1 and Appendix F.6). The additional latent-grid tests do not change dataset coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 3 adds MPP-S and pretrained MPP-L as comparators for diffusion-reaction; their Navier-Stokes entries are blank. Comparator membership in the original three benchmarks is retained. Extending the existing FNO, FFNO, transformer, and DPOT comparators to diffusion-reaction is separate from this limited baseline-family addition.

E3.justification: The existing training and rollout-evaluation design is retained, with task-specific additions. Appendix F.6 specifies diffusion-reaction data downsampled to 128 x 128 spatial points and 101 time points, a 900/100 training/test split, and a learning rate of 5e-4. Appendix F.4 adds three latent-grid configurations. The original benchmarks' stated splits, budgets, and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 Appendix F.4 and Table 6 add a focused robustness test asking whether the latent embedding grid must exactly match the dataset resolution. It compares 95 x 191, 97 x 193, and 128 x 200 grids against 96 x 192. Existing patch-size, embedding-type, grid-scale, interpolation-parameter, latent-width, and attention-head ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or experimental uncertainty estimates. Advection's mean, median, and worst-case summaries are retained; the new experiments do not introduce a different statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds a full diffusion-reaction results column: CViT-S/B/L achieve 1.13%, 1.11%, and 0.68% relative L2 error, respectively, versus 0.73% for fine-tuned DPOT-L (Table 3). Table 6 adds grid-robustness results ranging from 0.01562 to 0.01572. These are additional results, not improvements over v1 under the same settings. Original benchmark tables retain their values apart from equivalent rounding.

T1.justification: v2 adds Appendix E's Lipschitz definitions, initialization assumptions, coordinate-embedding theorem, and proofs comparing linear, Fourier, and Gaussian-grid embeddings. v1's FNO derivation is retained as Appendix D. The new analysis contains a substantive mismatch: Equation 21 studies an unnormalized Gaussian sum, whereas the architecture's Equation 1 uses normalized interpolation weights.

C1.justification: v1 foregrounds a unifying connection between neural operators and conditioned neural fields. v2 makes CViT and coordinate-embedding theory the central contributions, explicitly claiming spectral-bias mitigation and extending its performance claims to reaction-diffusion and larger pretrained models. The unifying perspective remains, but becomes supporting material rather than the leading contribution.

C2.justification: v2 introduces a substantial Lipschitz-based explanation of embedding performance and spectral bias, connects retained ablations to that explanation, and hypothesizes that Fourier features explain OFormer's advantage over GNOT. It also discusses DPOT's rollout-loss advantage and qualifies exact grid-matching guidance using the new robustness test. The original computational, data-scarcity, and geometry limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds diffusion-reaction equations, coefficients, data-generation details, and task-specific training information while retaining most implementation and timing details. It omits v1's explicit JAX vmap and grid-feature initialization descriptions. Its Reproducibility Statement replaces v1's direct public-code link with supplementary ablation code and a planned full release upon acceptance; the PDFs do not establish actual repository availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds substantial background and architecture-level comparisons with OFormer, GNOT, DPOT, and MPP, replacing v1's brief query-dependence contrast. New citations support spectral-bias theory, neural-field conditioning, and physics pretraining, including Rahaman, Rebain, and McCabe and colleagues. Several grid/interpolation antecedent references disappear, while the earlier neural-field survey is retained in the appendices.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled and extensively rewrites its abstract, introduction, architecture explanation, and discussion. v1 Sections 2–3 move into v2 Appendices B–C; the architecture is reorganized into sequential components. v2 adds dedicated related-work, future-work, ethics, and reproducibility passages and switches to author-year citations.

P2.justification: v2 redraws the architecture diagram to expose Perceiver aggregation, relocates conceptual diagrams to the appendices, and moves the model-configuration table into the main text. Previously appendixed rollout figures replace compact main-text snapshots. It expands the Navier-Stokes table with diffusion-reaction comparisons and adds a grid-resolution table and two diffusion-reaction rollout figures.

improvement.justification: The diffusion-reaction benchmark and grid-resolution test broaden empirical support, and the reorganized architecture description improves accessibility. However, the new central theoretical justification analyzes an unnormalized embedding rather than the normalized embedding actually specified in Equation 1. Documented code access also weakens from a direct link to an acceptance-contingent full release. These empirical benefits and theoretical/reproducibility concerns prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
